newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges shade higher on demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges shade higher on demand.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges began the week steady to a shade higher on relatively improved demand, traders said. High sulphur barges first traded at $82.75 a tonne fob ARA, or slightly above Friday's close, dipped to $82 before recovering again to the $82.50-$83 region.
"Demand is better than usual on Mondays," a second trader said.
The main seller in the market was a trading house that was said to have tried to put downward pressure on the market last week.
Bunkers were heard done at $85 a tonne for 380 CST material, $1 to $2 over Friday's levels, while 180 CST was talked at $1 higher at $89/$90.
Low sulphur barges were largely unchanged, quietly talked at $94/$96.

No early deals were reported in high sulphur cargoes but at least one cracked cargo was on offer. Price details were not immediately available but the cargo was on offer last week at a floating price equivalent to $77.50 fob.
Traders said a number of E-4 Russian straight-run cargoes were also being shown at premiums of $3.5 to $5 to three means.
